recipes.name: Kraft’s Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients_raw: 1.25 pounds red potatoes, cut into chunks
4 cups frozen mixed vegetables (carrots, corn, green beans, peas), thawed
0.75 cup BREAKSTONE'S Reduced Fat or KNUDSEN Light Sour Cream
0.5 cup KRAFT 2% Milk Shredded Sharp Cheddar Cheese, divided

steps.text: Cook potatoes and garlic in boiling water in large saucepan 20 min. or until potatoes are tender. Meanwhile, brown meat in large nonstick skillet. Stir in flour; cook 1 min. Add mixed vegetables, broth and ketchup; cook 5 min., stirring frequently.
Heat oven to 375 degrees F. Drain potatoes; return to pan. Add sour cream; mash until potatoes are smooth and mixture is well blended. Stir in 1/4 cup cheese.
Spoon meat mixture into 8-inch square baking dish; cover with potatoes.
BAKE 18 min. Top with remaining cheese; bake 2 min. or until melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Kraft’s Shepherd’s Pie
raw_recipe.description: This shepherd’s pie from Kraft is made with lean ground beef and has a light but flavorful layer of creamy mashed potatoes with Cheddar cheese on top.

review.reviewBody: this was really good !! as it was cooking i had my doubts. i added salt and pepper, and substituted PLAIN YOGURT for sour cream (much healthier) - the result was yummy.

Awesome recipe, although I made a few changes based on what I had in my pantry. Browned the ground beef, added a couple tlbspns of Bisquick instead of flour, a couple dashes of Worcestershire sauce & about 3-4 tblspns of Ketchup. I used half a small bag of frozen organic peas & half a small bag of frozen organic sweet corn (no carrots). Mixed together and put in the bottom half of my round Pyrex bowl. For the potatoes mixture, I drained 2 cans of whole potatoes & cut them up into cubes, added some milk and butter, used my mixer but not fully whipped. Poured them over beef mixture and then.covered with shredded cheddar cheese. Pyrex top on & into the oven it stayed for about 40 minutes. All I can say is YUM! Easy and a good hearty weeknight meal!

I made a cow's milk-free version of this recipe due to an allergy and it was very good! I used goats milk cheddar instead of regular, used sheep's milk pecorino - romano, chicken stock instead of milk and a buttery spread in the potatoes. The only reason I didn't give this a full 5 stars is because the meat mixture lacked flavor even after I sautéd onions before adding the meat. I needed to add quite a bit of salt and will absolutely add other herbs and garlic the next time I make it. But I will absolutely make it again!

This is my go to recipe for Shepherd's pie! Delicious all the time. EDIT: I forgot to add that I chop a bit of onion and cook it with the meat for extra flavor and use about 1 tbsp of tomato paste instead of ketchup. Edit 2: I have made this pie many times with my few modifications. This time, I decided to add a dash of Worcestershire sauce, one minced garlic clove, and 1/2 tsp of dried thyme. Results are even better! These additions raise the warm comforting food aspect of this one plate meal!

This is a very basic recipe so I added my own touch. I used salt and pepper, 1 1/2 tsp dry mustard,1 tsp garlic salt, 1/2 tsp coriander and 1/2 tsp fine herbs. I also sautéed the meat with 3/4 cup diced onins. To make life easier I also made instant potatoes in the microwave (adding more flakes than called for). I used low fat plain yogurt and 1 Tbsp low fat cream cheese in the potatoes. I'm sure if your making this recipe for a family you might keep it bland, but my husband and I enjoyed the additions I made.

I think this was a great starting point. I changed a few things. I didn’t put in the beef stock I substitute it for a can of cream of mushroom soup. I used instant potatoes because I didn’t have real ones so I put the sour cream in with the beef after it was cooked. I also didn’t have frozen veggies so I used a can of green beans a can of corn kernels and a can of sliced carrots. I added minced garlic onion powder garlic powder chili powder and Cajun powder to the beef while it was cooking to give it flavor and added pepper salt onion powder minced garlic to the potatoes to give everything more flavor because it seemed bland without it.!! After these few changes it was just like mom used to make.!!! Will definitely be making this again.! ??

I used peas/carrots, no corn since there's enough starch with the potatoes and personally feel the flavor is better. Added a layer of cheese after meat and didn't mix the veggies with the meat, layering the peas/carrots after the meat instead of mixing together and added some Worcestershire in the beef. I mixed an envelope of Knorr Beef Onion Soup Mix with the veggies before layering. I also used low sodium beef broth as I'm very sensitive to sodium taste. I added some other herbs such as rosemary and garlic to the potatoes while mashing and a little more low fat sour cream. It came out nice with the additions. :)

Just finished. So yes, salt and pepper it all. The potatoes were amazing following the recipe though I did taste and add salt and pepper. While the meat mixture was cooking, I read the reviews and promptly decided to add salt and pepper, sun dried tomato Mrs dash, splash of Worcestershire, minced dried onion, and garlic powder. I think maybe using gravy packet instead would be even better...or gravy itself. It's a good recipe to play with.

recipe sounded bland so I added lawrys seasoning salt, fresh black pepper a little Worcestershire and chopped 1/2 small onion. added to meat while Browning the meat. I love to cook in flavor. Also stirred in a little cheese before panning it up for baking. Smells delicious and the taste test was heavenly on the taste buds!

Love this recipe. Always get great reviews whenever I make it. I use whatever potatoes I happen to have around. When cooking the meat I add garlic, salt, pepper, onion powder, dill, and other seasonings that sound good at the time to help bring up the flavor. I also don't use four cups of veggies just a single bag of steamable veggies and it is plenty. Also, for the potatoes, I just make mashed potatoes like I normally would with butter and milk rather then using sour cream.

Very easy to make, had plenty for leftovers and my husband and I loved this. The only change I made was to add 1/2 a yellow onion which I sliced and sautéed before browning the ground beef. Will definitely make again!

Definitely a good base to start with. Always season the beef as it browns, adding the basic salt, pepper and garlic and maybe some oregano and thyme. I like to also add Worchester sauce to give the meat a rich flavor. Then I also add butter and sour cream, plus the basic SP&G to the potatoes.

This is a good base recipe but I definitely needs more flavor. It was very bland. It definitely had good potential if you maybe simmered the beef with an onion and added some salt, pepper, garlic powder & onion powder.
I cheated slightly, using leftover mashed potatoes and meatloaf but otherwise followed the recipe. Great
I loved it my fave comfort food...yummy. P.s.along i Add my own (x -tra Touch) ingredients ..
So easy to make & tastes just wonderful!

This was so good - I accidentally put a little more ketchup in it, put spring onions in with the meat, didn't put in the mixed veggies with the meat but put green beans on top of that before the potatoes and I think it was delicious! It's better than my mom's (shhhh, don't tell her). Sorry - I hate it when people give a recipe a high rating but then have had changed it all up but I think it would have been wonderful as is as well!
Super easy and everyone loved it. Only thing I added was some seasoning to the beef. Since it is so simple, it seems open to be able to add your own touches to it too.

I made this dish with ingredients we had on hand, so it's a bit modified. But it is absolutely DELICIOUS! You don't need exact measurements at all. We used chorizo instead of burger, added 1/2 onion and minced garlic to the browned chorizo and cooked about 10 minutes, then added 4 cups mixed frozen veggies (corn, peas and carrots). Also added about a cup of chicken broth, and 2 T cornstarch. We used baked, mashed sweet potatoes (3 large ones) for the mashed potato layer. Added sour cream and shredded cheddar. Best version we've had yet, but it's a personal taste of course.

Recipe was really easy but did make a few changes. To meat, browned with onions and garlic and I added salt, pepper, and other seasonings (tasted as I went). Used 2 1/2 tbs tomato paste to meat and broth instead of ketchup. Also added broth and let simmer before adding veggies. For mashed potatoes I used Philly cream cheese and salted butter. It turned out amazing.
